p:cNvPr.descr: An illustration of amino acid transformations at the alpha carbon that are facilitated by pyridoxal phosphate. In the transamination phase, it begins with L-amino acid, where C (in a pink box) bonds up to R, left to H, right to COO-, and down to +NH3. Below this is a plus sign. Below this is pyridoxal phosphate (internal aldimine form, on enzyme), where there is a hexagon with alternating double-bonded sides. The top right point bonds up, then down to P in a circle. The bottom point has NH (with a plus sign above). The bottom left point bonds down and left to H3C. The top left point bonds up and left to HO. The top point bonds up to CH, which double bonds up and left to H over N+, which bonds down and left to Lys, which bonds down and left to Enz in a blue oval. To the right of this are reversible arrows, indicating this as step 1: Formation of external aldimine with substrate. To the right of the arrows is Schiff base intermediate (external aldimine). It begins with C (in a pink box), which bonds up to R, right to COO-, left to H, which bonds down to +NH. To the top left is –B, which has two red dots beneath it and a red arrow pointing to H. A red arrow also points from the bond line from C to H to the bond line between C and +NH. +NH double bonds down to CH, which bonds down to the same pentagon explained in pyridoxal phosphate. In this pentagon, however, there are red arrows pointing from the double-bonded side on the top right to the single bonded side on the right. Another arrow goes from the double bonded side on the bottom right to +NH. To the right of this are reversible arrows, identified as step 2: Abstraction of proton, leading to quinonoid formation. To the right is quinonoid intermediate, which begins with C in a pink box, which bonds left to R, right to COO-, and double bonds down to +NH, which double bonds down to the same pentagon as above, with the exception that instead of a plus sign above NH, it has two red dots above. A red arrow points from those to the right bottom side. A red arrow points from the double-bonded right side to the single-bonded top right side. To the right of this are reversible arrows, identified as step 3: Rearrangement. To the right of this, it begins with C in a pink box, which bonds left to R, right to COO-, and double bonds down to +NH, which bonds down to the same pentagon as mentioned the first time, only instead of CH, CH2 is at the top of the pentagon. To the right of this are reversible arrows. Above these arrows, H2O merges with the arrow pointing right. This is indicated as step 4: Hydrolysis of Schiff base to form alpha-keto acid and pyridoxamine. To the right of this is alpha-keto acid, where C in a pink box, which bonds left to R, right to COO-, and double bonds down to O. Below this is plus sign. Below this is the same pentagon as described in the previous step, only CH2 bonds up to +NH3. This is identified as pyridoxamine phosphate. In the racemization phase, it begins with quinonoid intermediate, which begins with C in a red box, which bonds up to R, right to COO-, and double bonds down to +NH. A red arrow points from this double bond up to H+. +NH bonds down to CH, which double bonds down to C at the top of a pentagon. The top right point bonds up, then down to P in a circle. The bottom point is N over H with two red dots above, with a red arrow pointing from the to the bottom right side. The bottom left point bonds down and left to H3C, and the top left point bonds up and left to HO. The left side is double bonded. There is a red arrow pointing from the double-bonded right side to the single-bonded top right side. To the right are reversible arrows pointing to C in a red box, which bonds up to H, left to R, right to COO-, and down to +NH, which double bonds down to CH which bonds down to the same pentagon previously described in this phase, with the exception that instead of two red dots over NH, there is a plus sign. To the right of this are reversible arrows. Above these is Enz in a blue oval, which bonds up to Lys, which bonds right to NH3 (with a plus sign above N). This merges into the arrow pointing right to D-amino acid, where C in a red box bonds up to H, left to R, right to COO-, and down to +NH3. Below this is a plus sign, then pyridoxal phosphate (internal aldimine form, on regenerated enzyme). In the decarboxylation phase, it begins with the Schiff base intermediate as described above. To the right are reversible arrows, with an arrow jetting off the right arrow to CO2. To the right of the arrows is quinonoid intermediate where C in a red box bonds up to R, left to H, and double bonds down to +NH. A red arrow from this double bonds points to H+. +NH bonds down to CH, which bonds down to the same pentagon as described in the qiononoid intermediate above. There is a red arrow from that double bonds up to the bond line betweem +NH and CH. To the right of this are reversible arrows, which point to C in a red box, which bonds up to R, left and right to H, and down to +NH, which double bonds down to the same pentagon described in the second step in the racemization phase. To the right are reversible arrows as described in the last step of the racemization phase pointing to amine, where C in a red box bonds up to R, left and right to H, and down to +NH3. Below this is a plus sign, then below that is pyridoxal phosphate (internal aldimine form, on regenerated enzyme). To the left and bottom of the image is a white box showing the resonance structures for stabilization of a carbanion by PLP in brackets. To the left is carbanion, which begins with C with two black dots to the right in a pink box bonding up to R, left to H and down (this bond line is also in pink box) to +NH, which double bonds (in a pink box) down to CH which bonds down to the same pentagon described in the racemization phase. There is an arrow pointing left and right to the right of this. To the right of the arrow is quinonoid intermediate described in the decarboxylation phase, without the red arrows, and with C and its double bond down line in a pink box and the bond between +NH and CH is in a pink box.
